AWS states each Region consists of a minimum of three isolated, physically separate Availability Zones, each with independent power, cooling, and physical security, but does not break this down to individual facility addresses. This session confirmed this disclosure policy directly rather than assuming it, and applies this finding to AWS records that otherwise have no facility specific address, square footage, planned capacity, or critical_it_mw on file. reading.body:
AWS operates multiple data centers across Northern Virginia but does not publish power capacity, square footage, or specific building specifications as company policy. This facility is one building within the sprawling AWS campus footprint across Loudoun, Prince William, and Fairfax counties, collectively known as Data Center Alley. Because AWS withholds per-facility technical details for security reasons, this site cannot quantify this building's capacity in megawatts or derive how many racks or accelerators it hosts.

AWS committed $51.9 billion to Virginia between 2011 and 2021 and announced a further $35 billion investment through 2040 for new data center campuses in the state. Virginia handles approximately 70 percent of reported global internet traffic. Among Virginia facilities with published power figures on record, this campus ranks 24th by disclosed capacity, though that ranking reflects only the 23 facilities statewide that have released any megawatt figures; 326 mapped facilities exist in the state, meaning most operators publish nothing.

This facility cannot be assessed against the thesis that grid constraint binds AI scaling without access to its actual power capacity. Whether it matters to AI deployment depends entirely on AWS's unpublished allocation of critical IT load and its tie-in to the state's power infrastructure, neither of which AWS has disclosed.
